title: Balanced struggles keep communities uniform over long periods

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Balanced struggles keep communities uniform over long periods

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Although competition between organisms constantly recurs with shifting outcomes, the opposing forces are so finely balanced that community composition stays roughly the same for long periods, even though a trifling change could tip the balance toward one organism.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Battle within battle must ever be recurring with varying success; and yet in the long-run the forces are so nicely balanced, that the face of nature remains uniform for long periods of time, though assuredly the merest trifle would often give the victory to one organic being over another.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci Origin of Species claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1st ed., London: John Murray, 1859), Chapter III, “Struggle for Existence”; section “Complex relations of all animals and plants throughout nature”. Scope: natural communities of plants and animals

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on darwin1859-ch03-09: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.59

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Community stability is well represented in public time series, but the inferred mechanism and sensitivity to trifling changes are hard to distinguish from environmental stationarity. Present data resolve modern restricted versions.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Quantify long-term turnover and compositional stability in communities while measuring interaction-strength fluctuations, and test whether small perturbations predict persistent state shifts. Low net turnover despite fluctuating interactions plus high sensitivity would support the claim.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Most records are decades, not evolutionary long periods.

Fine balance of opposing forces is not directly observed.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
discriminating power: 0.41
data adequacy: 0.5
analysis feasibility: 0.64
operationalizability: 0.61
data existence: 0.78

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Community time-series archives can measure whether composition stays similar, which is half the statement and is already a standard analysis. They rarely include the trifling perturbation that would show the balance is easy to tip. Short duration, sampling noise, and the tension between the two halves keep the full wording only partly testable.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Quantify temporal turnover in community composition over long monitoring series, and, where perturbations exist, estimate how small a change shifts dominance. Long periods of low turnover would support uniformity; high sensitivity to small pushes would support the tipping clause; a series cannot support both clauses unless stability and sensitivity are given separate thresholds.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Most series span years to decades, not the long periods implied, and coarse taxonomy inflates apparent stability.

The statement combines long-run uniformity with hair-trigger sensitivity, which need different designs.

Apparent turnover is confounded with sampling error and observer change.
